pressReleaseTitle: India Ratings Upgrades B.G. Shirke Construction’s Bank Loans to ‘IND A+’/Stable
issuerName: B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd.
overview: India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) has upgraded B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd’s (BGSCTPL) bank loan ratings as follows:
overviewHTML:
The upgrade reflects the substantial improvement in BGSCTPL’s revenue, profitability and credit metrics in FY23, and the adequate liquidity available to support the growing scale of operations.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Ind-Ra continues to consider BGSCPTL’s standalone financials to arrive at the ratings along with factoring in the debt guaranteed for its wholly-owned subsidiary B G Shirke Redevelopment and Gas Pvt. Ltd. (BGSRGPL) and the likelihood of any incremental support required by BGSRGPL to arrive at the ratings.
keyRatingDrivers:
Strong Operating Performance, Further Ramp-up Likely from 1HFY25:  BGSCPTL’s operating revenue surpassed its pre-covid levels and grew to INR57.9billion in FY23 (FY22: INR43.9 billion; FY21: INR31.5 billion; FY20: INR38.79 billion), and its EBITDA increased to INR12.08 billion (FY22: INR6.78 billion; FY21: INR5.32 billion; FY20: INR 7.77 billion), due to the strong execution of its order book and increased contribution from its shipping segment. The EBITDA margin achieved pre-COVID levels of 20.9% in FY23 (FY22: 15.4%; FY21: 16.9%; FY20: 20.0%). BGSCTPL’s order book from construction contracts, which is the main line of business, stood at INR104.90 billion at end-July 2023 (end-May 2022: INR124.15 billion), providing order book visibility of about 2x of its FY23 revenues; additionally, it has been declared L1 in projects worth INR1.4 billion.

After having declined in FY22 on account of COVID-19, order inflows grew substantially over FY23-8MFY24 (INR35 billion in FY23; INR8 billion in 8MFY24 and L1 in INR 1.4 billion projects) owing to accelerated activity in the construction sector; furthermore, the company’s active bidding pipeline under consideration exceeds INR14 billion. Since a significant part of the orderbook was added during FY23-8MFY24, Ind-Ra expects a ramp-up in execution (post acquiring land and securing the required approvals) between 2HFY24-1HFY25. Ind-Ra expects the revenue to grow by 7%-10% yoy in FY24 and expects it to pick up further in FY25 due to the build-up of the orderbook; this shall be a key monitorable for Ind-Ra. Furthermore, the management expects the company to maintain similar margins in the near term.

Robust Credit Metrics: BGSCTPL's credit metrics improved in FY23 owing to the rise in EBITDA levels and decline in interest costs. The net adjusted leverage (including acceptances and outstanding against CG given) reduced to 0.30x at FYE23 (FYE22: 0.98x) and its gross interest coverage (operating EBITDAR/gross interest expense) increased substantially to 9.9x (4.5x). Ind-Ra expects the credit metrices to remain comfortable over the medium-term, supported by the projected operating performance and the working capital cycle.  The total outside liability (TOL) /EBITDA also reduced to 2.3x in FY23 (FY22:  4.19x), backed by healthy cash flows.

Healthy Free Cash Flows: BGSCTPL’s cash flow from operations (company-reported figures) increased to INR9.9 billion in FY23 (FY22: INR3.4 billion), driven by the increase in its revenue base and EBITDA. While the gross working capital to revenues decreased to 31% in FY23 (FY22: 36%), the current liabilities also reduced to 18% (28%), leading to the net working capital increasing to 13% of the revenue (8%). The reduction in current liabilities was primarily driven by a decline in mobilisation advances, since most authorities have started charging interest on mobilisation advances, making them less commercially-attractive; only Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority’s (MHADA) and City and Industrial Development Corporation’s (CIDCO) mobilisation advances do not entail an interest pay-out.  Ind-Ra expects the working capital levels to remain at FY23 levels over the medium term since the company is largely operating with a similar mix of counterparties. BGSCTPL incurred capex of INR5.6 billion in FY23, mainly for acquiring ships, and it expects to incur incremental capex of INR1 billion each year over the near term, which is likely to be funded by a mix of internal accruals and debt.

Liquidity Indicator - Adequate: Over the 12 months ended August 2023, the average utilisation of the company’s fund-based working capital limits was 33.5%, and the utilisation of its non-fund-based limits was 54.6%. The company’s fund-based and non-fund-based limits are largely from public sector banks. The on-balance sheet debt of INR11.11 billion at FYE23 comprised terms loan amounting to INR6.23 billion, working capital debt of INR4.01 billion and inter-corporate deposits from related parties worth INR0.87 billion. BGSCTPL had unencumbered cash and cash equivalents of INR8.28 billion at FYE23 (FYE22: INR4.7 billion), against scheduled repayments of INR2.29 billion and INR1.64 billion in FY24 and FY25 respectively, which are likely to be repaid from internal accruals. The agency believes that the low utilisation of fund-based limits and substantial cash balance provide strong balance sheet flexibility.

Exposure to Group Entities: As on 31 March 2023, BGSCTPL had extended corporate guarantees worth INR0.54 billion (INR0.62 billion in FY22) to group entities. Also, BGSCTPL’s gross loans and advances to its group companies increased to INR4.3 billion in FY23(FY22: INR4.0 billion), while net loans reduced to INR3.3 billion (INR3.4 billion), including write-offs of INR0.42 billion (INR0.59 billion). BGSRGPL, Shirke Recreation Enterprise, Parijat Hill View Realty LLP and Shirke Club Management LLP together accounted for about 78% of the total loans and advances provided by BGSCTPL in FY23. BGSRGPL had an outstanding gas division debt of INR3.4 billion (total debt of INR4.0 billion) at FYE23, for which BGSCTPL had kept in lien an equivalent amount of fixed deposit along with letter of comfort/undertaking, the management has informed the agency that aforesaid loans have been repaid by liquidating the fixed deposits. Now the gas division of BGSRGPL has been reverse merged into BGSCTPL. BGSRGPL is now engaged in the construction of three redevelopment projects in Mumbai region, which are under construction, and hence, might require intermittent support from BGSCTPL. Ind-Ra has factored the same in its analysis. Furthermore, the management expects a decrease in the loans and advances provided to two group companies, Parijat Hill View Realty and Teenmurthy Summit Realty LLP, as both projects have been completed. Ind-Ra does not expect any material fund outflows to support any group company operations in the near-to-medium term; the same shall be a monitorable.

Customer and Regional Concentration in Order Book Remains High: BGSCPTL’s order book is concentrated in terms of segmental as well as customer base. CIDCO and MHADA (including PMAY) account for 40% and 23%, respectively, of the orderbook, while the Central Public Works Department, Delhi Development Authority and Pimpri Chinchwad New Town Development Authority each account for about 7% of its total order book at end-July 2023. The concentration of the top 10 projects in the order book at end-July 2023 remained high at 73% (end-June 2022: 69%). The orders from Maharashtra, especially Mumbai Metropolitan Region and Pune together account for 83% of the order book, followed by Tamil Nadu (7%), Delhi (6%) and Karnataka (3%).  BGSCTPL continues to focus on the mass housing industry, wherein the company has a long track record and association with authorities.
ratingSensitivities:
Positive: Events that could, individually or collectively, lead to a positive rating action are:

·       Enhanced diversification in terms of segments, geographies and counter-parties

·       Structural changes that will elevate BGSCTPL’s governance structure maintaining a robust credit profile, with net adjusted leverage (including o/s CGs and acceptances) remaining below 0.75x and/or TOL /EBITDA remaining below 3.5x on a sustained basis. 

Negative: Events that could, individually or collectively, lead to a negative rating action are:

·       decline in profitability and/or elongation of the working capital cycle

·       material fund outflows to any group companies/ promoter payouts, leading to deterioration in liquidity

·       net adjusted leverage exceeding 1.25x and/or TOL/EBITDA exceeding 4.5x on a sustained basis
companyProfile:
Incorporated in 1994 (established business in 1944), BGSCTPL is the flagship company of the Pune-based Shirke Group. BGSCTPL is primarily engaged in the construction of housing projects for government agencies such as DDA, MHADA, CIDCO and Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana.

descriptionAboutIndiaRating:
India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) is India's SEBI registered credit rating agency committed to providing India's credit markets accurate, timely, and prospective credit opinions. Built on a foundation of independent thinking, rigorous analytics, and an open and balanced approach towards credit research, Ind-Ra has grown rapidly during the past decade, gaining significant market presence in India's fixed income market.

Ind-Ra currently maintains coverage of corporate issuers, financial institutions (including banks and insurance companies), finance companies, urban local bodies, and structured finance and project finance companies.

Headquartered in Mumbai, Ind-Ra has seven branch offices located in Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Gurugram, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Pune. Ind-Ra is recognised by the Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India.

Ind-Ra is a 100% owned subsidiary of the Fitch Group.
